absent: Single origin and scatter gather DMA debug mapping, unmapping and sync behavior beyond inert fallbacks, including entry lifecycle and error reporting.
Complete DMA debug entry layout, other type markers besides noncoherent, and helpers for entry allocation, insertion and unmap checking.
Driver filter storage duration, default content, bound value and matching against devices.
Direct translation helpers for encrypted and plain paths, forced decryption detection, mask and limit provenance, and bus address to physical conversion.
Bounce slot release, background growth worker, transient reclamation worker, usage counters and high water semantics.
Coherent pool sizing, refill worker, availability threshold and zeroing guarantees for other allocation paths.
Device bounce state setup, pool list lifetime, lock ordering with other device locks, and teardown.
Numeric values for slot size and shift, segment size, page order limits, alignment masks and error sentinels.

findings.text: Page based tracking offers hook debug_dma_alloc_pages that records a noncoherent entry for a device transfer and hook debug_dma_free_pages that checks unmap against an equivalent reference. Both hooks do nothing when global debugging is disabled, and allocation also does nothing when entry reservation fails.

Early boot handler dma_debug_driver_setup installs a driver filter name into a bounded current name buffer, stopping at string end or bound, then emits an informational message when a nonempty filter was supplied. It always reports successful handling to the init parser.

Fallback header supplies inert inline variants for physical mapping, unmapping, scatter gather mapping, unmapping, coherent allocation, release, single and scatter gather synchronization for central processor and device, plus page allocation and release. Each variant accepts the normal device and transfer descriptors and performs no action.
Debug header defines include guard macro _KERNEL_DMA_DEBUG_H that prevents multiple inclusion.

Direct mapping helpers expose computation dma_direct_get_required_mask from maximum physical extent, translation dma_direct_to_page from bus address, validation dma_coherent_ok for coherent memory, and selection phys_to_dma_direct between encrypted and plain paths driven by device forced decryption state.

Optimal allocation zone is chosen from the smaller nonzero value among device coherent mask and bus limit, converted to a physical ceiling. Ceilings at or below the low zone threshold select the lowest zone, ceilings at or below the thirty two bit threshold select the middle zone, otherwise no zone flag is added.
Coherent addressability holds only when translation of the physical origin succeeds and the full extent including size stays within the smaller nonzero value among coherent mask and bus limit.

Physical to bus translation branches on an unencrypted request flag, delegating to the plain path when set and to the protected path otherwise. Callers derive that flag from whether the device forces unencrypted operation.

Direct coherent allocation helper dma_direct_alloc_swiotlb obtains a page from the bounce allocator then revalidates coherent addressability. When validation fails the page is returned to the bounce layer and allocation reports failure.

Changing memory protection for coherent buffers may fail. On failure to drop protection or to restore protection the code emits a rate limited warning and deliberately leaks the memory rather than using mismatched protection.
Default low DMA zone ceiling is a twenty four bit mask and is marked read only after initialization.

Page tracking record carries field type set to the noncoherent marker, field dev set to the owning device, field paddr set to physical origin, field size set to transfer length, field dev_addr set to bus address, and field direction set to transfer orientation. Allocation populates a fresh entry while release builds a temporary for validation.

Bounce allocation entry swiotlb_alloc takes device plus size plus attributes, locates device bounce memory, requires matching shared mode, reserves aligned slots, then returns the page for the slot origin. It fails when memory is absent, mode mismatches, no slots remain, or the slot origin is misaligned.
Shared mode must agree between bounce memory or pool state and allocation request attributes. Mismatched requests are rejected before any slot or pool search.

Slot arithmetic derives slot count by rounding up over slot size, slot address by shifting index and adding base, segment offset by masking within segment length, maximum slots from boundary mask shifted, area wrap by resetting at area length, area count capped by slots per segment, and alignment offset from device minimum mask combined with caller mask and slot granularity.

Slot reservation first scans existing areas starting from current processor with per area offsets, then when nothing fits and growth is allowed it schedules background expansion and attempts an emergency single area pool sized to the request. Success marks device bounce use and publishes the pool choice with ordering guarantees, while oversize requests or disabled growth fail immediately.

Area search holds the area spin protection with interrupt state saved while checking availability and while installing allocation results. Transient pool insertion holds the device bounce list protection with interrupt state saved. Pool list traversal for search runs under read side critical section against concurrent reclamation.

Bounce pool record stores field cc_shared for sharing mode, field vaddr for virtual base, field area_nslabs for per area quota, field nareas for partitioning, field late_alloc for timing, field end for physical ceiling, field start for physical base, and field nslabs for total. Each area stores field used plus field index plus field lock. Each slot stores field pad_slots plus field alloc_size plus field orig_addr plus field list. Initialization zeroes the data area and sets list from segment remainder, orig_addr to invalid sentinel, and counters to zero.

Pool creation caps slab demand to a page order limit with area adjustment, reserves pool metadata, then repeatedly attempts buffer reservation while halving demand on failure until minimum is reached. Slot metadata is then reserved, the pool is initialized, and failures release prior reservations and report absence.

Buffer reservation prefers the atomic coherent pools when the request cannot block and sharing is required, otherwise it clears zone flags and selects low or thirty two bit zone from the physical ceiling. Allocation retries with progressively lower zones when the address exceeds the ceiling, and fails when no zone satisfies the limit.

Coherent pool interface offers allocation dma_alloc_from_pool that iterates candidate pools and returns the first fitting page with zeroed content, plus release dma_free_from_pool that scans candidates for address ownership and returns ownership status. Both iterate through a guessing helper that prefers pools matching zone hints.

Pool guessing starts from zone hint using pools atomic_pool_dma and atomic_pool_dma32 and atomic_pool_kernel, preferring low then middle then kernel order for low hint, middle then low then kernel order for middle hint, and kernel then middle then low order otherwise, skipping absent pools. Continuation from kernel moves toward middle, continuation from middle moves toward low, and continuation from low ends.

Per pool allocation reserves from the generic pool, translates to physical, validates through an optional caller predicate with refund on rejection, schedules background refill when availability drops below threshold, zeroes the result, and returns its page.
When candidate pools exist but all are exhausted, allocation warns unless the caller suppressed warnings. When no candidate pool exists at all, allocation always warns. Both cases return failure.

Release from coherent pools scans candidates in default guess order and frees through the first pool that owns the address range, reporting success. When no pool owns the range it reports failure without side effects.
When slot reservation yields a bus origin that is not page aligned, allocation emits a one time device warning identifying the offending address, releases the reserved slots, and fails.
Pool area search treats zero slot demand and out of range area selection as fatal programming errors.

Area search enforces slot granularity on caller alignment, preserves page granularity for large requests without explicit alignment, honors device segment boundaries and minimum alignment against original address, strides by the larger of caller and device alignment, fails when demand exceeds free space, updates predecessor free runs and next search position on success, and accounts usage.
Transient usage accounting and high water accounting each have two build variants, one that records the slot count and one that does nothing, selected at compile time.
Emergency pools are marked transient, linked into the device pool list, and counted in transient totals. Failed emergency search schedules deferred reclamation through read copy update work.

Buffer release first attempts return to a coherent pool and succeeds when owned there. Otherwise it restores encryption when sharing required tearing down only on success, and leaks intentionally when protection cannot be restored.

Page reservation for bounce buffers allocates the required order, rejects results whose end exceeds the physical ceiling with a retry signal, drops protection when sharing is required, and on protection failure attempts to restore protection before either freeing or intentionally leaking.
